corrected_claim: The date claim is wrong as printed and is replaced. The National Park Service Administrative History (Unrau 1991) says: "After the battle Meade had detailed him to make the first survey and map of the field in October 1863", and lists "Cope, Emmor Bradley. 'Battlefield of Gettysburg, Pa., 1st, 2nd, & 3rd of July, 1863.' (October 1863)"; Georg (NPS, 1981) calls it "E. B. Cope's 'horseback' survey map of the battlefield in October 1863" and the Little Round Top CLR names it the "Cope (horseback survey)". So the map is dated October 1863; no reachable source gives "August" for Cope. The words "August ... 1863" belong to a different map: an NPS study says S. G. Elliott's map was "surveyed sometime between August and November of 1863". Further documented: the Cope map shows lines of breastworks (NPS-EISE-CLR1, Fig. 1.3, "1863 Cope Map indicating line of breastworks"; the NPS Record of Treatment: "The Cope Map depicts a Confederate redoubt on the high point at the western edge of Houck Field"); a post-battle map "based on survey by Major E. B. Cope" is reproduced from Atlas to accompany the Official Records plate XL (= Atlas plate 40, listed in the Atlas index for Gettysburg, map 2); the park holds a copy of Cope's map from RG 77 at NARA ("Copy on file ... Archives"); LOC 99447498 is a blue-print "Gettysburg battlefield" by Cope and Hewitt dated 1863 (1 print, blue, with Confederate positions hand col. in red, 44 x 26 cm, scale ca. 1:26,000). Not established: that LOC 99447498 is the same work as NARA E 105a-1; the NAID 176246318; Warren's annotation text ("mostly from horseback sketches based on the map of Adams County"); the scan itself.

corrected_claim: The NPS statement is verified verbatim: "Our most important mapping resources included Department of War and Gettysburg Battlefield Memorial Association maps prepared in 1863, 1868, and 1872".
